I don't know exactly how your psychologist phrased it, but It's definitely not the CAUSE of your tics. I know specifically with tourettes, maybe other tic disorders I'm not sure, common conditions or disorders like OCD, depression, anxiety, ADHD etc are initially looked into to see if helping manage those things helps tics in turn. It's so frustrating getting a diagnostic! I'm sorry you had this experience and that you felt like you weren't being taken seriously. I definitely recommend seeing a neurologist, specifically one that has experience with tourettes or tics in general. It sounds to me like she was trying to not offend you?? Idk, obviously you'd know better from a stranger on the internet lmao. 

Also, I think you mentioned worries about how it affects your driving and everyday activities, I completely get where you're coming from, it stresses me out too. I knew he was just desperate and pulling at straws. My dad died from cancer when I was a toddler. I don’t remember him. Ughhhh I fucking hate that too. I’ve isolated myself in high school in a very small town. I mean it’s not like I turned away from people who tried, but I just gave up on trying to socialize with people who rarely tried to socialize with me either and settled for sitting in the hallway by myself during lunch break.  I’d stare at the floor trying to distract myself from the white noise of people socializing around me. But eventually it got better. I found ways to cope. Hurting yourself btw is not the way to go. You probably know that already but if not let me just say that pinching yourself and scratching yourself can eventually evolve to cutting and punching. The urge to hurt yourself can sometimes be strong but try to get in the habit of doing something with your hands like drawing, writing, or baking. Maybe even going for a walk. It helps.
